answer: An AI agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with a slashable bond tied to a unique physical anchor: to register, an agent locks collateral and proves custody of a distinct asset, say a timber lot, a meadow plot, or a summit relay site. The ledger records each anchor once, so no one can reuse it. Caught signing two conflicting histories, an identity loses its bond. To field k fakes, an attacker must buy k distinct anchors and lock k bonds; cost rises linearly while any single reward stays fixed, so more identities mean more expense, not more payout, and the swarm is priced out.
